3 By this petition, filed under Articles 226 and 227 of the Constitution of India, the petitioner seeks directions against the respondents to pay compensation as per the provisions of the National Highways Act, 1956 (hereinafter referred as 'the Act of 1956') in respect of the land admeasuring 20 R from Survey No. 5/3 of Mouza Bodkha,
Tah. Patur, Distt. Akola, acquired for widening of Akola-Nanded National Highway under Road Namrata 3.wp.6261.2022 judge.odt Widening Project.
4
The respondent No. 4 had issued notification dated 10.08.2016 under Section 3-A of the Act of 1956 to acquire the land for the purpose of widening Akola-Nanded National Highway.
Objections were called for under Section 3-C of the Act of 1956 and upon hearing the persons interested in the Sau.

2 land a final report was submitted and the notification was issued under Section 3-D of the Act of 1956 that the land would be acquired for the purpose of widening of the Akola-Nanded National Highway.
5 The petitioner was not paid any compensation in respect of the land admeasuring 20 R from Survey No. 5/3 on the premise that the said land is gaothan land owned by the Government.
The petitioner made several representations to the competent authority disputing that the said land admeasuring 20 R is a gaothan land.
The petitioner brought to the notice of the competent authority that the land was recorded in the survey records in his name.
The petitioner claimed that the acquired land Namrata 3.wp.6261.2022 judge.odt is part of his ancestral property and being the absolute owner he is entitled to receive the compensation.
Pursuant to the representations made by the petitioner fresh joint measurement were carried out and report was drawn wherein the land was held to be navin gaothan.
Ultimately, the claim of the petitioner came to be rejected.
Hence, this petition, for the relief as stated above.
6 At the outset, it would be relevant to refer to certain relevant provisions of the Act of 1956.
Section 3-A confers power on the Central Government to acquire land required for the building, maintenance, management or operation of national highway or part thereof.
Section 3-B confers power to enter the property for survey, measurement, valuation and all other acts specified in the Section.
Section 3-C provides for hearing of objections and decision thereon.
Then follows the declaration of acquisition under Section 3-D and power to take possession and right to enter the acquired land in terms of Section 3-E and 3-F of the Act of 1956.
Section 3-G confers powers on the competent authority to determine the amount payable as compensation.
The Namrata 3.wp.6261.2022 judge.odt factors which are to be taken into consideration for determining the amount are set out in sub-section (7) of Section 3-G of the Act of 1956.

Sub Section (5) of Section 3-G provides that if the amount determined by competent authority under sub-section (1) or sub section (2) of Section 3-G is not acceptable to either of the parties, then, the amount shall, on application by either of the parties, be determined by the arbitrator to be appointed by the Central Government.
7 Section 3-H, which relates to deposit and payment of the amount, is relevant to decide the matter in hand.
Sub Section (1) of Section 3-H imposes obligation upon the Central Government to deposit the amount determined under Section 3-G with the competent authority before taking possession of the land.
Upon deposit of such amount, the competent authority shall on behalf of the Central Government, pay the amount to the person or persons entitled thereto.

Sub-section (3) of Section 3-H provides that where several persons claimed to be interested in the amount deposited under sub-section (1), the competent authority shall Namrata 3.wp.6261.2022 judge.odt determine the persons who in its opinion are entitled to receive the amount payable to each of them.

Whereas sub-section (4) stipulates that if any dispute arises as to the apportionment of the amount or any part thereof or to any person to whom the same or any part to thereof is payable, the competent authority to refer the dispute to the decision of the Principal Civil Court of original jurisdiction within the limits of whose jurisdiction the land is situated.
Sub- sections (5) and (6) deal with the interest payable on the excess amount determined by the Sau. Rekhatai W/O Govindrao Tayade vs Union Of India, Thr.

3 arbitrator and deposit of excess amount with interest with the competent authority.

8 A plain reading of the aforesaid provisions reveals that the Act of 1956 confers powers on the competent authority to determine and disburse the compensation to the person who claim to be interested in the amount deposited under sub-section (1).

If the quantum of compensation is not acceptable to the parties, the competent authority, on an application filed by either of the parties, is under an obligation to refer the parties to the arbitrator to be appointed by the Central Government.

Similarly, whenever any Namrata 3.wp.6261.2022 judge.odt dispute arises as to the apportionment of the amount or any part thereof or to any person to whom the same or any part is payable, the competent authority is under an obligation to refer the dispute to the decision of the Principal Civil Court of original jurisdiction.

In other words, whenever there is dispute raised by any person as to the right to receive either the whole or part of the compensation, the competent authority has no other option but to refer the dispute to the Principal Civil Court of original jurisdiction and such dispute has to be decided by the Court.
9 In the instant case, admittedly the petitioner had disputed that the acquired land is a gaothan land and claiming to be the absolute owner, he had claimed right to receive the entire compensation.

It is also on record that the internvenor -Ashabai Rathod had also raised dispute and claimed compensation in respect of the land admeasuring 20 R from Survey No. 5/3 situated at Mouza Bodkha, Tah. Patur, Distt. Akola.
It is thus evident that there is dispute as regards the ownership of the acquired land and the right to receive the compensation in respect of the acquired Namrata 3.wp.6261.2022 judge.odt land.
The competent authority cannot be directed to pay compensation to the petitioner unless such dispute is resolved.

Nevertheless, considering the fact that the petitioner had raised a dispute, the competent authority, in terms of sub section (4) of Section 3-H was under an obligation to refer the dispute to the Principal Civil Court of original jurisdiction.

10 In such circumstances the petition is disposed of with direction to the competent authority to refer the dispute raised by the petitioner as well as by the intervenor, in respect of the land admeasuring 20 R from Survey No. 5/3 situated at Mouza Bodkha, Tah. Patur, Distt. Akola, to the decision of Principal Civil Court of original jurisdiction, as contemplated sub-section (4) of Section 3-H of the Act of 1956 within a period of three weeks from the date of receipt of this order.
11 Rule accordingly.
No costs.
(VRUSHALI V. JOSHI, J.) (ANUJA PRABHUDESSAI, J.)
